style: Say clearly and steadily, like a trusted radio news reader
lines: Welcome to the fact-check desk. Every chart here was published. Tap a clue tool, like Ruler, to find out what it's hiding.
Tap a second bar, picture, or point. The ruler compares the picture to the numbers.
Clues go in your notebook. When you know the trick, pick it, rule on the headline, and press File it.
Filed. Now turn on the switch in Fix it to correct the chart.
Not quite. Recheck the clue tools named in the hint, revise your ruling, then press File it again.
All six cases are closed. Press Spin Room to see how the tricks are made.
Now you work for the client. Move the spin controls to give them their wish, and watch the meter.
This is what a fact-checker would catch. Press Make it honest to undo every trick.
Use the clue tools to collect a measurement before filing. A ruling needs evidence from this chart.
